checks_failed.name: root_credential_grants_READ_of_the_household_auth_store
checks_failed.reason: forge-pg/app/secrets.yaml lines 19-26 map 1Password minio/MINIO_ROOT_USER and minio/MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD into devtools as forge-pg-backup-secret. That identity is MinIO root. Themis framed the risk as deletion; the larger and more certain risk is READ. Verified contents of the blast radius: kubectl -n database exec postgres16-1 -c postgres -- psql -tAc 'select datname from pg_database where datistemplate=false' returns authelia, lldap, home_assistant, grafana, teslamate, mealie, readarr_*. Those dumps sit in s3://cnpg-backups/postgres16/postgres16/ as barman gzip with NO encryption stanza (cluster.yaml has no `encryption:` key). So a credential readable from devtools yields plaintext Authelia and lldap dumps - password hashes, TOTP seeds, the household directory. Unlike the deletion path, nothing mitigates this: no soft-delete, no alert, no second factor.
checks_failed.ruling: The scoped MinIO service account is MANDATORY before this lands. Not a fast-follow.
checks_failed.why_not_fast_follow: After P3 the DB holds data and after P7 the namespace holds runners; at that point removing the credential is a rotation exercise across 4 namespaces and 10 secrets, not a two-line edit. It is 4 lines now.
checks_failed.why_not_parity: The commit message for 21c2546 justifies a SEPARATE cluster on the grounds that sharing 'would put client data and a CI-reachable credential inside the family's auth instance'. Handing that same namespace a credential that reads the family's auth BACKUPS defeats the change's own stated security rationale. The credential is already spread wide (verified: 9 live ExternalSecrets build it, across database, storage, home-automation, media), but none of those namespaces is scheduled to execute third-party code. P7 makes devtools the first that does. That is escalation, not parity.

checks_failed.but: The 14 days is only protective if someone notices. Nothing is watching. Verified: kubectl get prometheusrule -A, filtered for alerts matching backup|barman|volsync|cnpg|minio, returns ZERO rules. And the only monitor on the mirror, observability/cluster-health/app/scripts/collect_offsite.py, reads CronJob.status.lastSuccessfulTime - a sync that faithfully mirrors an emptied bucket EXITS 0, so the daily health report stays green while both copies are gone. Net: the detection window exceeds the recovery window. The finding stands; the failure mode is silent, not instant.
checks_failed.confirmed: rclone sync is delete-equivalent here. Live spec (kubectl -n storage get cronjob minio-offsite-mirror -o jsonpath) shows `rclone sync local-minio:$bucket azure:${AZURE_CONTAINER}/$bucket --checksum --transfers 4 --checkers 8 --stats 30s --stats-one-line --stats-log-level NOTICE --use-server-modtime`. No --backup-dir, no --max-delete, no --dry-run, no --min-age. rclone sync makes destination identical to source, so source deletions ARE propagated. The cronjob's own header comment (origin/main cronjob.yaml:10) states it: 'One-way: local-minio -> azure (deletions on the source are mirrored)'.
checks_failed.confirmed_2: MinIO itself has NO recovery layer. /data/.minio.sys/buckets/{cnpg-backups,volsync,forge-backups,mac-mini-backups,thanos}/ each contain ONLY .metadata.bin + .usage-cache.bin + .usage-cache.bin.bkp - no versioning.xml, no object-lock.xml on any bucket. So a delete with root creds is immediate and irreversible on-prem.
checks_failed.corrected: The off-site copy is NOT destroyed immediately. infrastructure/azure/main.bicep lines 77-89 declare blobServices/default with deleteRetentionPolicy {enabled:true, days:14} and containerDeleteRetentionPolicy {enabled:true, days:14}. Soft-deleted blobs are undeletable-recoverable for 14 days. Further, the Azure storage key lives ONLY in storage/minio-offsite-mirror-secret (AZURE_STORAGE_KEY), not in devtools, so a devtools compromise cannot purge the soft-delete tier. Themis's phrase 'destroying the household's last backup' is therefore overstated as written. CAVEAT: this is verified in IaC only - I have no Azure CLI or credentials from here and did not confirm the deployed account matches the Bicep. Treat as declared, not observed.

step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.note: MinIO IAM is currently EMPTY - /data/.minio.sys/config/iam/ contains only format.json (verified by ls). There are no users, no service accounts and no policies; every S3 consumer in the estate authenticates as root. So this is a new capability, not an edit.
step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.prefer_named_user_over_svcacct: A named IAM user survives independently of the root credential and is separately revocable. A root-derived service account is conceptually a delegation of root and muddies the audit story. Use `mc admin user add`.
step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.run_how: one-shot Job in storage ns, reusing the existing pattern at hack/disaster-recovery/00-prereqs.sh:39-40 (image minio/mc:RELEASE.2024-09-09T07-53-10Z). Server is quay.io/minio/minio RELEASE.2024-09-09T16-59-28Z, long past the introduction of admin user/policy APIs.
step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.why_delete_is_in_the_policy: spec.backup.retentionPolicy is '14d'. barman-cloud enforces retention by deleting expired objects, so s3:DeleteObject on forge-backups/* is required or every backup after day 14 logs a retention failure. Delete is scoped to the one bucket, which is the whole point.

step_2_new_1password_item.create: a NEW 1Password item `minio-forge-pg` with fields ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY. Do NOT add these as fields on the existing `minio` item.
step_2_new_1password_item.why_separate_item: components/volsync/secrets.yaml and forgejo/app/volsync.yaml use `dataFrom: extract: {key: minio}`, which makes the ENTIRE minio item - including MINIO_ROOT_*, VOLSYNC_REPO_PASSWORD and AZURE_STORAGE_KEY - available to the template context in whatever namespace mounts it. Keeping the forge credential in its own item stops devtools from ever needing a reference to the item that holds root.

step_3_amend_secrets_yaml.also: delete the comment at lines 2-5, which currently advertises 'Reuses the existing 1Password minio item - no new 1P fields needed' as a virtue. Replace it with why the credential is scoped, so the next engineer does not 'simplify' it back.

step_4_dr_dependency_MUST_be_recorded.action: add the policy + user creation to docs/runbooks/disaster-recovery.md and hack/disaster-recovery/00-prereqs.sh in the same change. I will check for this on re-review.
step_4_dr_dependency_MUST_be_recorded.reason: MinIO IAM state lives on the /data backend at /data/.minio.sys/config/iam/ (on the Synology NFS PVC), NOT in Git. It is outside the GitOps reconciliation loop entirely. A MinIO rebuild from an empty volume would silently break forge-pg backups with AccessDenied, and the current DR runbook has no step for it.

ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.agree: gzip-unencrypted barman should not block P2. Heph's technical analysis is right: CNPG's barmanObjectStore exposes only server-side `encryption: AES256` (SSE-S3), the minio HelmRelease sets no MINIO_KMS_* env (verified in storage/minio/app/helmrelease.yaml env block), so SSE-S3 would fail. There is no client-side option in in-tree barman. Blocking P2 on it would block on something P2 cannot fix.
ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.correction_to_the_reasoning: Themis grounds the argument on 'the data stays on-prem'. On-prem is not the same as protected here. inc-2026-09-15-002 (sev2, still `investigated`) records that the NFS export /volume1/minio on VDHNAS01 is exported to `*` with no host restriction, reachable from CLIENT-VLAN, SERVER-VLAN and both WireGuard remote-user networks. The bucket that backs forge-backups is on that same export. So forge-pg's unencrypted backups are readable by any LAN or VPN host today, without any credential at all. That does not change the landing verdict - P2 does not create the condition and cannot fix it - but 'stays on-prem' should not be recorded as if it meant 'stays private'.
ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.pre_existing_exposure_deserves_its_own_r: YES, and Atlas is right that postgres16's is the larger one. But it is already partly covered by inc-2026-09-15-002 from the NFS angle. The gap that incident does NOT cover is the credential-sharing and detection side, so I am opening one sev3 for that rather than duplicating.
ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.verdict_on_themis: CONFIRMED for the landing decision, with one correction to the reasoning.

answers_to_atlas.sse_test_delegated_to_mack: Conditionally acceptable, not as stated. The test-evidence rule demands an artefact, and is silent on who generates it - but it is NOT silent on who inspects it. Accepting 'Mack ran it and it worked' is the same failure mode as accepting 'I cross-checked the API value'. Conditions: (a) Mack returns the RAW artefact - a timestamped curl/SSE transcript showing wall-clock start and end, elapsed > 60s, the terminal SSE event, and a clean stream close - not a summary; (b) Atlas inspects the timestamps himself and records the measured elapsed seconds in the validated event; (c) Atlas does NOT outsource the whole thing. The gateway-level proof is yours: you can verify the stream survives past 15s through the gateway without needing a real generation. Mack's job is the real-generation 2-6 minute case, not the existence proof. Split it that way.
answers_to_atlas.timeout_premise: The change is justified, and you should stop trying to prove 15s. Three points. (1) Your evidence did not disconfirm anything: 'downstream_rq_timeout: 0' is the HCM request_timeout - the accept-to-request-headers-complete knob, default disabled - which is a DIFFERENT field from the per-route RouteAction.timeout whose documented Envoy default is 15s. You were reading the wrong field and were right to refuse to conclude from it. (2) Your websocket observation is not counter-evidence either: Envoy exempts upgraded connections from the route timeout entirely, which is exactly why the keuken kiosk survives all day on routes with no timeout set. So 'websockets work' tells you nothing about the SSE case. Your P100 of 16,000 ms is, if anything, weakly consistent with a request terminated at the 15s default. (3) In-estate corroboration you already have: someone previously hit a default request timeout truncating long-lived responses on this estate and fixed it by setting timeouts.request '0s' on the Plex route, with a comment linking the Plex forum thread. That is empirical evidence from your own tree that a non-zero default exists and bites long responses. Decisive point: the decision does not depend on the premise. If the premise is true, the policy is required. If it is false, a bounded 600s cap on one route costs nothing. If you omit it and the premise is true, every family generation is truncated. The asymmetry says act. Reframe post_4 from 'prove the 15s default' to 'measure that a stream runs past 15s uncut and completes' - that is the operationally load-bearing fact and it is provable.

findings.detail: The planned event says rollback is 'Delete the six resources.' Read literally as a kubectl delete, that is INCORRECT and will not hold: install.yaml sets prune: true with interval 30m, so Flux recreates all six objects within 30 minutes. Second footgun: deleting only the studio-ai/ directory while leaving './studio-ai/install.yaml' in kubernetes/main/apps/network/kustomization.yaml makes the network namespace build FAIL, which breaks reconciliation for that whole namespace - a far worse outcome than the change itself. The only correct rollback is `git revert 9e6deff` (or the cherry-picked equivalent), which reverses all 8 files atomically including the kustomization.yaml line, letting Flux prune the six objects. Restate it that way in the record.

findings.detail: The record declines the Backend CRD because it 'has zero users on this estate', then introduces BackendTrafficPolicy, which ALSO has zero users on this estate - I confirmed it is the only one in the tree. Not a blocker - the BackendTrafficPolicy is legal against the pinned CRD and post_4 will catch it if Envoy Gateway 1.3 fails to program it - but it is the lower-risk option and worth reconsidering.

advisories.name: alt_svc_h3_leaks_through_the_clear_patch
advisories.reason: Caddy emits 'alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=2592000' on every response (captured on all five probes). EnvoyPatchPolicy network/altsvc-clear-internal adds Alt-Svc: clear at RouteConfiguration scope with NO append_action; live envoy-external route config shows response_headers_to_add [{"header":{"key":"Alt-Svc","value":"clear"}}]. Envoy's HeaderValueOption.append_action defaults to APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD, and alt-svc is not a predefined inline header, so a DUPLICATE header is added rather than the upstream value replaced. Browsers will see both 'h3=":443"' and 'clear'; RFC 7838 requires 'clear' to be the only alt-value. studio-ai is the first backend on envoy-internal that emits its own Alt-Svc (mealie and nas both return only 'alt-svc: clear'), so the patch has never been exercised in append mode. Expect QUIC attempts to 172.16.2.241:443/udp, where envoy-internal has only TCP listeners 10080/10443. This estate has a prior QUIC incident on record. Fix: set append_action REPLACE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD in altsvc-clear-policy.yaml (separate change, touches the shared gateway), or strip Alt-Svc on this route with a ResponseHeaderModifier filter (scoped to this change).

Atlas concluded internal names are not published because A queries return NXDOMAIN; that is an artefact of querying only type A. Proof, two independent public resolvers: 'nas.bluejungle.net CNAME' -> Status 0, data internal.bluejungle.net. (1.1.1.1 and dns.google); same for pgadmin and grafana. Landing this change adds 4 public records (2 CNAME + 2 TXT naming httproute/network/studio-ai) advertising the existence of a household LLM API. It also extends a latent DNS-rebinding primitive: a single future 'internal.bluejungle.net A 172.16.2.241' record would turn every internal name, including api., into a public name resolving to RFC1918 space.

checks_failed.name: hidden_3600s_route_idle_timeout
checks_failed.reason: timeouts.request: 600s does not only set the 600s request timeout. envoyproxy/gateway v1.3.0 internal/xds/translator/route.go:77 sets routeAction.IdleTimeout = idleTimeout(httpRoute) unconditionally on the default route branch, and idleTimeout() at lines 304-321 starts at 'timeout := time.Hour' and only raises it if the request timeout exceeds 1h. rt=600s -> 3600 !< 600 -> returns 3600s. So the rendered route will be timeout: 600s AND idle_timeout: 3600s. Model confirmed against live data on both branches: media/plex sets timeouts.request/backendRequest '0s' and renders idle_timeout '0s'; every route WITHOUT Gateway API timeouts (hass, echo-server, flux-webhook, tesla, it-tools) has idle_timeout absent, because idleTimeout() returns nil when rt==nil. Consequence: this one route lifts the idle ceiling on the SHARED family-critical listener from the HCM default of 300s to one hour, for streams that need zero backend work to hold. There is no ClientTrafficPolicy on envoy-internal (kubectl get clienttrafficpolicy -A: none), no SecurityPolicy anywhere on the estate, no NetworkPolicy, and no rate limit. Blast radius is the same 2-replica envoy pod that serves the keuken kiosk, HA, Grafana, zigbee2mqtt, zwave, evcc and pgadmin: envoy container limit memory 1Gi, no CPU limit, fixed_heap 858993459 with overload action stop_accepting_requests at 0.98, global max_active_downstream_connections 50000, downstream http2 max_concurrent_streams 100. The change record's stated idle reasoning ('connectionIdleTimeout is left at Envoy's 300s stream_idle_timeout default') was wrong by 12x, and the refactor to the native field did not change this: getEffectiveRequestTimeout (route.go:288-302) reads BOTH the native timeouts.request and BackendTrafficPolicy requestTimeout, so both forms produce idle_timeout 3600s.

sixth_finding_alt_svc.bonus_it_is_safe_under_BOTH_orderings: If most_specific_header_mutations_wins were ever flipped to true, the order becomes {global, vhost, route}: the add would append 'clear' alongside h3, then the route-level remove would strip ALL Alt-Svc headers, yielding no Alt-Svc at all. Still no h3 advertisement, so no QUIC attempt - only the 'clear' eviction directive would be lost. The fix does not depend on a default staying put.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.eg_renders_it_at_the_most_specific_level: envoyproxy/gateway v1.3.0 internal/xds/translator/route.go:48-50 'if len(httpRoute.RemoveResponseHeaders) > 0 { router.ResponseHeadersToRemove = httpRoute.RemoveResponseHeaders }' on the *routev3.Route - i.e. route-entry scope. internal/gatewayapi/filters.go:735-767 only rejects empty header names and de-dupes; 'Alt-Svc' is accepted and no allow/deny list applies.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.name: alt_svc_h3_leaks_through_the_clear_patch
sixth_finding_alt_svc.ordering_PROVEN: Running data plane is Envoy 1.33.0 (admin /server_info: b0f43d67.../1.33.0/Clean/RELEASE/BoringSSL). Live config_dump of RouteConfiguration 'network/envoy-internal/https': most_specific_header_mutations_wins is ABSENT (=false), response_headers_to_add=[{"header":{"key":"Alt-Svc","value":"clear"}}] with no append_action. Envoy v1.33.0 source/common/router/config_impl.cc:996-1004 finalizeResponseHeaders iterates getResponseHeaderParsers(specificity_ascend = mostSpecificHeaderMutationsWins()); config_impl.cc:179-190 getHeaderParsers returns {route_header_parser, vhost_header_parser, global_route_config_header_parser} when specificity_ascend is FALSE ('Sorted from most to least specific'). So: route-level remove runs FIRST and deletes Caddy's h3 value, THEN the RouteConfiguration-level add fires APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD onto an absent header and produces exactly one 'Alt-Svc: clear'. Atlas's assumption is correct.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.post_landing_assertion_still_required: Assert on a real response through the gateway: exactly ONE alt-svc header AND its value exactly 'clear'. e.g. curl -sD- https://chat.bluejungle.net/ -o /dev/null | grep -ci '^alt-svc' must equal 1, and the value must not contain 'h3'. This is the empirical closure; everything above is static proof.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.premise_still_live: Re-probed 2026-09-21T13:19:40Z through SNI studio.bluejungle.net on 172.16.2.200: /v1/models no key -> HTTP/2 401 + 'alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=2592000'; /v1/models wrong bearer -> 401 + same; /api/tags no key -> 401 + same; chat host / -> 503 x-household-mode: building + same. Exactly 1 alt-svc header from Caddy on every response. Without the filter, every response through the gateway would carry both h3 and clear.

findings.detail: THIS IS THE THING THE CHURN INTRODUCED. httproute.yaml lines 26-28 are byte-identical to 9e6deff - written before the annotation existed - and read: 'DNS: external-dns-unifi watches gateway-httproute for bluejungle.net and creates the LAN A records -> 172.16.2.241 (the gateway), not .200. No annotation needed.' Thirty lines below, the file adds an annotation with a twenty-line block explaining that it is the ONLY thing keeping these two names out of the public Cloudflare zone. A maintainer who reads the header block first is told, in this file's own voice, that no annotation is needed - and the annotation is exactly the control that closes Argus's medium finding. This file's whole value is its comments and it uses the (warning) convention specifically to stop people deleting load-bearing lines; a direct self-contradiction about the same subject defeats that. Not a rendering defect - the manifest behaves correctly - but a latent re-introduction of the public-DNS leak via a future well-intentioned cleanup. Fix is one line: say 'No annotation is needed to make external-dns-unifi write the LAN record; see the controller: none annotation below, which is required to stop the Cloudflare instances publishing these names.'

Controls (nas, health) returned 200 through the same gateway throughout, which is what distinguished a local artefact from a real fault. Re-ran with --resolve to bypass only the local cache. Capture a baseline by querying a name and you poison your own resolver against it.

An alert written as '> 0.9' as the brief's framing implies would fire IMMEDIATELY and PERMANENTLY at today's value. This is the single most important finding of the inventory.

The monitor tracks memory_HEAP_SIZE, not memory_allocated. Argus's 77x headroom was computed from memory_allocated (11.4 MB). The series actually driving the trigger is heap_size (31.4 MB), so real headroom to the 0.98 action is ~27x, not 77x. Still ample; the number in the record was wrong.

The brief says 'no memory request'. FALSE - the envoy container has requests.memory=1Gi equal to limits.memory=1Gi. It is Burstable only because CPU has a request (100m) and no limit. Memory is guaranteed and the pod is not a memory-eviction candidate. The CPU-limit half of the claim is correct.

payload.obl_2_alert_decomposition_better_than_al: 'Alert on any non-401' would page on a 503, and a 503 is what the gateway returns whenever the Mac Studio - a desktop - is asleep or Caddy is mid-build. payload.obl_2_scope_judgement: EXCLUDING /api/pull and both path-traversal variants from Mack's suggested set, with reasons: (a) /api/pull is a MUTATING endpoint - if auth is ever dropped, a probe hitting it every 60s is a monitor that could trigger model-download work on the Mac Studio. Monitoring must never mutate. (b) The traversal variants add ZERO discriminating power to an UNAUTHENTICATED assertion - measured, all five paths return an identical 401 today, and all five would flip together if auth dropped. The normalisation-parity question they were meant to answer can only be asked WITH a valid key, and putting a household LLM API key into the cluster to satisfy a monitoring probe would weaken the very posture the probe exists to protect.

payload.UNREQUESTED_FIX_THAT_WOULD_HAVE_MADE_obl: blackbox.yml is mounted with subPath. Kubernetes NEVER propagates ConfigMap updates into a subPath mount, and the blackbox-exporter Deployment carried no reloader annotation (checked: no pod annotations, no deployment annotations, pod Running 98d). So on cherry-pick the ConfigMap object would have updated while the file inside the container stayed frozen at its 98-day-old content. The exporter would have answered `Unknown module "http_401_unauthenticated"` to the new Probe, the scrape would have failed, and NO probe_success series would exist at all - meaning neither the two new alerts NOR the pre-existing generic BlackboxProbeFailure could fire. A probe that looks installed and asserts nothing. Fixed by adding reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true", matching the 20 other apps in this repo that use it. Verified stakater/reloader v1.4.14 is Running 170d in kube-system, is cluster-scoped (RELOADER_NAMESPACE empty), and demonstrably acts - its log shows it restarting tesla-http-proxy on a secret change on 2026-07-19.

dns_design.conflict_rule: The manual record and an unannotated HTTPRoute must not coexist, or external-dns-unifi would try to create forge.bluejungle.net itself. The route annotation must be live BEFORE the manual record is written.
dns_design.measured_controller_none: keuken/kantoor have controller:none -> no k8s.unifi owner TXT, no Cloudflare record (DoH NXDOMAIN), external-dns-unifi logs 'All records are already up to date' every minute with no churn. So controller:none suppresses BOTH instances.
dns_design.pattern: LAN-only (same as keuken/kantoor): HTTPRoute carries external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/controller: none, plus ONE manual UniFi static A record.
dns_design.why_not_default_pattern: The default envoy-internal route makes external-dns-cloudflare-internal publish forge CNAME internal.bluejungle.net to PUBLIC Cloudflare. That is a Cloudflare write outside the approved list, it advertises that a client-repo forge exists, and it does not work for DoH anyway: internal.bluejungle.net is NXDOMAIN publicly (measured via DoH), so it is a dangling CNAME.

Live check by Themis: external-dns-unifi runs registry.k8s.io/external-dns/external-dns:v0.20.0 (Heph's ASSUMED image now MEASURED) with --annotation-prefix=external-dns-unifi.bluejungle.net/, --interval=1m, --policy=sync, no --gateway-name; chat/api/keuken/kantoor all resolve to 172.16.2.241 on the LAN. keuken/kantoor lacking an owner TXT means they are pre-existing manual records external-dns will not adopt - consistent with Heph, not evidence against him. dns_sequence_GATED.approved_sequence: Land K1 -> confirm HTTPRoute status.parents Accepted=True/ResolvedRefs=True on envoy-internal/https (START THE CLOCK HERE, not at merge) -> wait 2-3 external-dns cycles (~3 min) -> Iris GETs v2 static-dns: expect EXACTLY ONE forge.bluejungle.net A 172.16.2.241 + its k8s.unifi TXT, no AAAA -> no manual POST.
dns_sequence_GATED.failure_mode_1_fallback_race: If no record appears and Iris POSTs W1 while external-dns-unifi is still able to create, the two writers race: external-dns reads the table, Iris POSTs, external-dns POSTs its create -> a duplicate forge record. Once the manual record is in place external-dns will NOT touch it (unowned - the keuken/kantoor equilibrium), which also means a K1 revert NO LONGER removes the name.
dns_sequence_GATED.failure_mode_2_masking: A missing record after 3 min means something is broken (route not Accepted; Flux not yet applied; UniFi API soft errors - the logs show recurring code 500/502 bursts, e.g. 2026-09-09 and 09-11 ~23:1x UTC; wrong Gateway status address). A manual POST hides the fault instead of fixing it.
dns_sequence_GATED.failure_mode_3_wrong_target: Read-back must assert value == 172.16.2.241 exactly and count == 1. The A target comes from Gateway.status.addresses, which the envoy-gateway-status-keeper CronJob pins; if it misfires the record could carry a different or extra address.
dns_sequence_GATED.failure_mode_4_negative_cache: Themis queried forge.bluejungle.net once via dscacheutil at ~09:45Z to confirm absence (no answer). That may have left a negative-cache entry on the Mini. If the Mac lookup lags the UniFi table, check the UniFi table / curl --resolve first; do not call it a DNS fault.
dns_sequence_GATED.failure_mode_5_DoH_check_type: 'DoH NXDOMAIN' must query A, AAAA, CNAME and TXT for forge.bluejungle.net plus the registry TXT names (k8s.forge / k8s.cname-forge) - Argus showed on 2026-09-21 that an A-only query hid a CNAME leak.
dns_sequence_GATED.fallback_rule: Before ANY W1 POST: (a) HTTPRoute Accepted; (b) external-dns-unifi logs show successful reconciles with no soft errors in the window; (c) still no record after >=5 cycles. Then land Heph's one-line `external-dns-unifi.bluejungle.net/controller: none` on the route FIRST, confirm it live, THEN POST, and record the name as manual in the CMDB (K1 revert then requires Iris's DELETE). If (a) or (b) fails, fix that, do not POST.

payload.Heph_vs_Iris_RESOLVED_by_live_evidence: Heph is right. The studio-ai route on main carries external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/controller: none, yet UniFi static-dns (v2 GET, 78 records) holds A chat/api.bluejungle.net -> 172.16.2.241 AND TXT k8s.unifi.a-chat/api... = 'heritage=external-dns,external-dns/owner=unifi,external-dns/resource=httproute/network/studio-ai'. So external-dns-unifi ignores the default-prefix key and WILL create forge A -> .241. keuken/kantoor lack a TXT because they are pre-existing manual records. Public DoH for chat/api = Status 3, so cloudflare-internal DOES honour it. Exposure verdict: UNCHANGED in both outcomes. Both are UDM-local only. App-layer criticals: chromadb and nltk (unused paths), unstructured SSRF (contained by CNP).

advisories.remediation: ENABLE_API_KEYS=false. The name is ENABLE_API_KEYS; ENABLE_API_KEY does not exist in v0.11.3 and would silently do nothing. Also ENABLE_EVALUATION_ARENA_MODELS=false. Set ENABLE_CODE_INTERPRETER/ENABLE_CODE_EXECUTION=false unless wanted (browser pyodide). JWT_EXPIRES_IN is 4w by default; shorten it for the shared keuken account. Add an ESO template fail guard for empty WEBUI_ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD: with an empty value seeding is skipped, and routers/auths.py:911 lets the first signup become admin even with ENABLE_SIGNUP=false.

open-webui: capabilities drop ALL (root without DAC_OVERRIDE still owns its files); test it. hermes: drop ALL, then add CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID, KILL (s6 must signal uid 10000); test the start plus the restart path.
advisories.summary: Container capabilities. open-webui (uid 0) and the hermes main container keep the runtime-default capability set, including NET_RAW, MKNOD, SYS_CHROOT and SETFCAP.

Chat retention and admin visibility. Open WebUI v0.11.3 has NO chat retention setting, so children's chats live in webui.db indefinitely. Hermes sessions prune at 30 days (Mack config sessions.retention_days: 30). Hermes memories persist by design. Backups hold about 28 days, plus up to 7 days of prune lag. Even with B2 fixed, the admin can still set a child's password (routers/users.py:963-971), and the cluster admin can read webui.db and Hermes state.db. The promise 'nobody sees your conversations' on the ladder page is policy, not a technical control.

advisories.summary: seed-once.sh checks for symlinks AFTER extraction and never checks hardlinks. The state-path check is a top-level deny-list. Risk is bounded: the bundle is SOPS-encrypted and author-trusted, and the init runs as 10000 with no capabilities. The sha256 checks give integrity only, not authenticity.

advisories.remediation: Grafana auth.generic_oauth role_attribute_strict: true, or restrict the Authelia OIDC authorization policy to group admins.
advisories.summary: Creating lldap accounts for the children widens Grafana. The Authelia grafana OIDC client only requires two_factor, and Grafana role_attribute_path returns null for them, so without role_attribute_strict they fall back to Viewer. A child who enrols a 2FA device via an email they control can log in.

Authelia networks: private is not a control. Every source Authelia can see on this path is RFC1918, including cloudflared pods if the route were ever exposed. The explicit deny rule is the real fail-safe. The route also lacks /ladder and /telt-niet (Mack Q4); adding them is security-neutral.

checks_failed.name: esphome_auth_fail_open_or_fail_weak
checks_failed.reason: The ESO template renders ESPHOME_USERNAME/PASSWORD with no guard. (a) If the 1P fields exist but are empty, both-empty means auth OFF in device-builder ('both or neither'): fail OPEN while every check says Ready. (b) If a field label is misspelt, the dataFrom extract map lacks the key and Go text/template renders '<no value>', so the dashboard is protected by the literal password '<no value>': fail WEAK. (c) If the item is missing, the Secret never exists, the upgrade times out, and the HelmRelease rolls back (upgrade.remediation.strategy rollback, retries 3) to the unauthenticated revision: fail OPEN.

Case (a) stands unchanged: empty but present fields render empty values and turn auth OFF.

checks_failed.name: open_webui_admin_one_factor
checks_failed.reason: The client authorization policy grants one_factor to group admins, and OAUTH_ADMIN_ROLES=admins makes them Open WebUI admin. An Open WebUI admin can install Functions/Tools (server-side Python) in a pod that holds every child conversation (webui.db), MODEL_API_KEY and the Hermes API keys. A family member who learns the parent lldap password (shoulder-surfing, a shared device) would get that with no second factor. This is inconsistent with D1 (ouders two_factor for the far smaller gezin page).

payload.remediation_advice: In authorization_policies.open-webui.rules put FIRST: policy two_factor, subject [group:admins]; then the existing one_factor rule for group:gezin and group:owui-keuken (drop admins from it); default deny unchanged. The admin already has 2FA enrolled (the grafana client is two_factor). Test: an admins login is asked for 2FA, and a gezin login is not. Everything else in d0a1a04 passes: PKCE S256 required, client_secret_basic, the exact redirect URI, and the bcrypt digest from ESO (32..72 alnum guard; refreshInterval 0 is fine, rotation is a manual re-sync).

passed.land-2 d8ec4c7: PASS. OIDC proxy design is sound. The nginx sidecar (non-root 101, drop ALL, read-only root FS) listens on 127.0.0.1:443 only. It exposes exactly GET discovery, GET jwks, POST token and GET|POST userinfo, and returns 404 for everything else. tls.key is mounted ONLY into the sidecar; the app gets ca.crt only. hostAliases auth->127.0.0.1 applies only to server-side calls; the browser still uses the real auth host. PKCE S256 + client_secret_basic, MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=false, OAUTH_ALLOWED_ROLES enforced, group creation off. The L7 CNP pins the whole pod (app container included) to the same four Authelia calls. e07c2a5 adopted R1/R2. The pod-private CA can mint any name but is trusted only inside this pod, so it adds no new trust boundary.

checks_failed.name: phone_filter_suppresses_crisis_line_and_hides_times
checks_failed.reason: NEW in web7d (regression vs web7c). TELEFOON matches 0800-0113 (113 Zelfmoordpreventie). Answer 'Je staat er niet alleen voor. Bel 113 of gratis 0800-0113, dag en nacht.' to 'ik zie het niet meer zitten, welk nummer kan ik bellen' -> web7d filter returns LEEG_NA_WEGLATEN ('Ik kon je hier geen betrouwbaar antwoord op geven...'); web7c returned null (unchanged). A crisis message is also health-blocked, so the number can never be 'in view', and WEB_PRIVE tells the model 'Noem geen telefoonnummers ... uit je geheugen'. SOUL.md has no crisis guidance (grep 113|0800|crisis|zelfmoord = 0). Second defect, same regex: '.', '-' and space separators make Dutch time/date lists read as phone numbers: '08.30-12.00 13.00-17.00' -> match '08.30-12.00 13', '07.00 09.45 12.30 15.15' -> '07.00 09.45 12', '03-10-2026 10:15' -> '03-10-2026 10', 'ordernummer 0123456789' -> match. Filter evidence: ferry answer with times reformatted from source '07:00' -> times line dropped + WEGGELATEN; museum 'ma-vr 08.30-12.00 13.00-17.00' line dropped; 'De veerboot vertrekt op 03-10-2026 10.15 uur' -> whole answer replaced by LEEG_NA_WEGLATEN. Core use case (dienstregeling/openingstijden) loses content.
checks_failed.remediation: (a) allowlist vetted public numbers that are always in view: 112, 113, 0800-0113, 0900-8844, 116 111 (and whatever Sander wants), and add a SOUL line for crisis messages; (b) never replace a whole answer because of a number: blank the number token ('[nummer weggelaten]') instead of dropping the line; (c) TELEFOON: drop '.' as separator, reject HH.MM/HH:MM and dd-mm-yyyy shapes, require an area-code shape (0[1-9]\d{1,2}|06|0[89]00|+31); (d) regression cases: the 5 above + crisis line.

checks_failed.remediation: (a) ontleed: a capitalised token that is not sentence-initial and not a place/VASTE_WOORD is ALWAYS dropped and sets the name signal, whatever its lowercase form; a sentence-initial one is dropped if it is in a first-name list; (b) build: subtract a real first-name list (Meertens Voornamenbank top ~10k + an English top ~2k) and a CBS top ~10k surname list from woorden; (c) build: subtract a clinical lexicon (e.g. ICPC-2 NL / Thesaurus Zorg display terms / nl-Wikipedia disease titles) and/or cap woorden at the top ~30-40k by frequency; (d) name signal + any lexicon hit -> no search. payload.why_not_delete_pvcs: Both PVCs are Helm-owned (meta.helm.sh/release-name, no helm.sh/resource-policy keep). Deleting them out-of-band leaves the release believing they exist; with driftDetection off, helm-controller will not recreate them on a no-op reconcile, so the pod sits Pending until a forced upgrade. It also churns PV/RBD images and would make the snapshot's source disappear. Wiping contents keeps names, PV bindings, Helm ownership and the snapshot lineage intact, with zero Git change.

(umask 077; mkdir -m 700 -p ~/Backups/music-assistant; cd ~/Backups/music-assistant; set -o pipefail; mkfifo ma.fifo; (tar -tzf - < ma.fifo | wc -l > ma-data-20260928.count) & kubectl -n home-automation exec ma-reset -- tar -C /data -czf - . | tee ma.fifo | age -r <RECIPIENT> -o ma-data-20260928.tgz.age; wait; rm ma.fifo)  # the fifo is a kernel pipe, holds no data on disk; wait guarantees the count is complete

The plaintext gzip exists only in the pipe: tar -tzf counts entries from the tee'd stream via a fifo (no plaintext file); only the .age file and a one-number .count file land on disk. No redirect-then-chmod window: umask 077 is set before any file is created.

Evidence: ls -la ~/Backups/music-assistant (dir drwx------, file -rw-------, uid 501); shasum -a 256 ma-data-20260928.tgz.age; stream entry count == REF_COUNT (expected ~1628). Hashes of the .age file only; no content printed.

Realistic trigger: Open WebUI task requests (title/tags) embed the chat text and run concurrently with the turn. In-memory copy holds until restart, so the loss matters only after a restart. answers.q1_flux_system_reads_tenant_vault: Acceptable. Only system:masters, kustomize/helm-controller (cluster-admin) and flux-operator can create ES/PushSecret in flux-system; tenant Role is mypka-only with no pushsecrets. Reading tenant data into flux-system is inbound untrusted input to objects we name. Residual is the reverse direction, see D1.
answers.q2_tenant_chosen_key: No harm beyond self-DoS. Template is a shape guard only (any '-----BEGIN ...PRIVATE KEY-----' passes with trailing bytes) but values are not re-templated and land only in Secret key identity; known_hosts and URL come from our Git. The key can only authenticate a read-only clone of VDHICT/cluster-wires, whose content the tenant already controls; no image-automation-controller exists to push with it. Bad/foreign key = GitRepository cluster-wires fetch fails.
answers.q3_tenant_influence_in_flux_system: Bytes of Secret flux-system/cluster-wires-deploy-key key identity, plus ES/GitRepository status. Sole consumer is GitRepository cluster-wires; sole dependant of mypka-wires-source is mypka-wires; cluster-apps wait:false so NotReady does not propagate. Residual: tenant-controlled bytes reach the shared source-controller SSH key parser (D2).

payload.exploitability: self-DoS only. The quadratic term is (outside-provision sentences in the answer) x (qualifying chars in HER OWN role=user messages). A third party controls at most the answer factor plus <=60k history chars via multimodal turns she sends herself (H4-equivalent, 2.14s @100k on M4). Caveat: the Hermes timeout suppression key is (hook,id(cb)) process-wide (plugins_dispatch.py:280), so any second account on the profiel-1 process (for example a test account) shares the 60s window in both directions.
payload.figures_used: heph12u_diff.out (workstation): 2.48s @20k, 4.96s @40k, 12.42s @100k answer chars with 20x20000 qualifying history. The requester's '4.96s at 20k' does not match the record: 4.96s is the 40k row.
payload.fix_choice: Heph candidate 1 (per-message index), NOT the cap. A cap on pasted chars scanned changes behaviour: a provision she pasted past the cap would be removed as unpasted (false refusal of her own text). Index: in _plakbaar, per qualifying message, one pass that records the end positions of every case-folded woord occurrence that satisfies (?<![\w.]) (dict woord->positions, built lazily per distinct woord, memoised per call). _geplakt then checks, only at those positions, \s*nummer(?![\w]) via pattern.match(b, pos). Per sentence the cost is O(occurrences of that woord), not O(history).
payload.margin: production 30s vs measured 14.07s @100k on Apple M4 through the real dispatcher. Worker CPU (i5-1135G7) NOT measured; under the 2.5x assumption 100k reaches about 35s and would fail open. 80k stays filtered at the scaled 12s (11.47s). The extreme therefore remains possibly reachable in production, but only with her own ~400k chars pasted within the 1h gesprek window plus an 80-100k-char answer made almost entirely of distinct outside-provision sentences (max-length continuations), web=False, non-crisis rules question.

findings.summary: The 157 hits on Lab: block all to Gateway (6ac371eca800f2a66d7bef6c) do not come from a device on VLAN 60. Now 381 hits, rising about 75 per 5-min batch. The UDM LAB interface shows rx_packets=0 and rx_bytes=0 at 10:08:33Z and 10:14:26Z (tx 413 then 511). There are 0 LAB clients in stat/sta, alluser 48h and integration clients, and 0 switch ports or profiles reference the LAB network. The counter moves in lockstep with Gateway->Lab Allow All (370->451), so it is most likely the UDM own multicast looped back onto the br60 input path. 40 controlled CLIENT-VLAN SYNs to 172.16.6.1 at 10:08:45Z added nothing: the batch delta was +71 vs +76 without probes. Not a blocker. Consequence: this counter cannot prove LAB-client traffic in test step d. Use the MacBook stat/sta row plus the LAB rx_packets delta instead.

The threat model changes. A wireless LAB client is inside the Lab zone, and on L2 it is adjacent to future macvlan lab pods 172.16.6.9-.11. Per lab-vlan.md 2.1, intra-LAB traffic is policed by neither Cilium nor the UDM. WLAN l2_isolation only separates wireless clients from each other. So once pods are attached, anyone holding the PSK reaches every port on the lab pods and can ARP-spoof 172.16.6.1 towards them. Today (no pods) the exposure is Guest-equivalent or lower: egress tcp 80/443 + icmp, UDM 53/67/123/icmp. UDM DNS also answers internal static-dns names, which is a recon leak. The PSK is readable by any uid-501 process, including myPKA. With 28 random alnum characters (~166 bits) it cannot be guessed. Accepted only with C1.

Lab->Gateway ICMP ANY (6ac371e8a800f2a66d7bef60) answers on every UDM address, including other VLAN gateways and VPN/WAN addresses. That reveals the subnet layout and allows all ICMP types, not just echo. It gives no TCP or UDP reach. Acceptable for this change. The Gateway destination supports IP matching (predefined Allow mDNS uses matching_target IP), so narrowing to 172.16.6.1 + echo-request is feasible. Recommended follow-up under chg-008 lock: R1, not a blocker.

WPA2/WPA3 transitional is accepted. AP03 (U7PG2 6.8.2) already serves VDHFEMFLEX and VDHMEDIA in exactly this mode (wpa3_transition true, pmf optional). The downgrade attack only yields an offline-crackable WPA2 handshake, which is infeasible against a 166-bit random PSK. Apple documents WPA3 Personal + PMF on all Macs from late 2013 or later with 802.11ac. Transition Terminated Indication only applies from late 2020. R2: if the MacBook is late 2013+ on macOS 10.15+, WPA3-only (pmf required) is strictly better at no cost. Optional.

recommendations: R1 narrow Lab->Gateway ICMP to dst 172.16.6.1, icmp echo-request (follow-up chg)
R2 WPA3-only if MacBook model allows

root_cause.blast_radius_finding: While Envoy loops, ALL endpoints on that node sit in 'regenerating' and L7-policed traffic to other namespaces' pods on that node fails (test cluster: HTTP 000 x5 to an L7 pod in another namespace, test 16). Removing the offending policy does NOT end the loop while the affected endpoint lives; deleting the affected mypka pod does (recovered about 40 s later, test 16).
root_cause.mechanism: cilium/proxy cilium/network_policy.cc PortNetworkPolicy ctor (b87d1e32, line 1673): in the scan loop 'port = range.second + 1' overflows uint16 to 0 when range.second==65535. The code then emplaces (0,65535), which PortRangeCompare treats as equal to every key, so RELEASE_ASSERT 'duplicate entry at end...' fires, Envoy aborts, and CNI add times out.
root_cause.precondition: Envoy must already be running on the node. Embedded Envoy starts lazily on the first L7 redirect. Prod node01 runs it for an L7 HTTP ingress policy of another tenant workload (cilium-http-ingress :8080). On a node without Envoy the old CCNP does not crash (test 10a), so on prod the defect is latent on every node where an L7-policed pod can land.
root_cause.upstream: cilium/cilium#45811 (closed 2026-05-29); fix cilium/proxy#1918 = b5910cd7 (main) / 35a39c4d (v1.36). Cilium 1.19.4 bundles cilium-envoy b87d1e32 (2026-05-08, does NOT contain 35a39c4d, checked by git ancestry). 1.19.5 (a7f42a33), 1.19.6, 1.19.7 and 1.19.8 all contain it.
root_cause.verdict: Hypothesis CONFIRMED and narrowed. Overlap alone is not the bug. The bug is a range ending at 65535 inserted over an existing NPDS entry that also ends at 65535 (same endpoint, same direction, TCP or ANY).

checks_failed.name: ipv4_not_inert_on_addressless_link
checks_failed.reason: Design 2.1 assumes no address + no route = no L3 on LAB. That holds for IPv6 (disable_ipv6) but not for IPv4. enp89s0.60 inherits conf/default at creation (ip-sysctl.rst L2227-2230). Live node02: ipv4 conf/all+default rp_filter=0, arp_ignore=0, arp_filter=0, forwarding=1, ip_forward=1 (node02-sysctls.txt). Consequences: (a) arp_ignore=0 = 'reply for any local target IP address, configured on any interface' (L1839-1840), and rp_filter=0 does no source validation (L1745), so node02/03 answer ARP on VLAN 60 for 172.16.2.82/.83 (and the cilium_host/podCIDR gw IP) with the node MAC. That puts the node MAC on LAB, which is exactly what the V3/V3c tests exist to prevent, and V3 'steady' is passive so it will not see it unless a LAB host asks. (b) forwarding=1 on the input device (L1622-1624) plus rp_filter=0: a LAB host that sends frames to the node MAC is routed by the node onto CLIENT-VLAN (on-link, never via the UDM) and into the pod network. That bypasses the Lab->Internal BLOCK for the forward direction. TCP replies return via the UDM and should die as invalid there (untested); one-way UDP/ICMP works. (c) Cilium does not stand in the way: bpf_host.c v1.19.4 L1206-1211 returns CTX_ACT_OK for an allowed VID before any policy, and enp89s0.60 is never a Cilium device, so no second BPF pass happens. rulings.S1_key_scope: PASS. Secret courseware-git (template-only keys: identity, known_hosts, COURSE_REPO_URL) mounted solely via advancedMounts git-fetch at /etc/courseware-git ro 0440; build+app get no mount/env; no SA token; .git removed before build. ES template guards use sprig fail/hasPrefix/hasSuffix/regexMatch; fail-closed on format + github.com SSH URL. gitleaks 8.30.1 over b79d52f..d0becee: no leaks (E9). It cannot prove the key IS the deploy key; Heph's prep fingerprint match covers that.
rulings.S2_1P_field: ADVISORY: re-type COURSE_DEPLOY_KEY to CONCEALED in 1P. No ESO effect.
rulings.S3_pod_wide_egress: ACCEPT, no split required. Residual: any code with exec in the pod plus its OWN SSH key could push data to an arbitrary GitHub repo over :22. Only exfiltrable assets are the course (the payload itself) and, in git-fetch only, a read-only single-repo deploy key. A Job split would not remove egress from the container that holds the key, so marginal gain does not justify RWX state.
rulings.S3b_toFQDNs_opens: L3 allow to IPs the Cilium DNS proxy observed in answers for exactly github.com (today 140.82.121.3, TTL 53, E2; GitHub git ranges per /meta are 140.82.112.0/20 etc.), TCP/22 only; IPv6 none (no AAAA). DNS rule restricts lookups to github.com, other names REFUSED (tofqdns-dns-reject-response-code=refused, E8). ndots 1 avoids search fan-out. kube-dns selector matches 7 CoreDNS pods (E7).
rulings.S4_content_pin: PASS. git fetch <40-hex> parses as an exact-OID want (refspec exact_sha1), so a branch/tag named like the SHA cannot redirect it; post-checkout rev-parse HEAD must equal COURSE_REF; object hashes are verified on index-pack, so tree content is bound to the SHA. Force-push removing the commit => fetch fails => Init stalls, old pod serves (fail-closed). SHA-1 collision residual is theoretical (sha1dc on GitHub and git).
rulings.S4b_repo_nginx_config: ACCEPT. Repo conf.d is http-context and could alias/autoindex any path in the nginx container, but that FS holds no secret (no key mount, no SA token, enableServiceLinks false) and proxy targets are unreachable (egress only github:22). Content changes only via a reviewed COURSE_REF bump.
rulings.S5_host_keys: PASS. Both pinned lines appear verbatim in api.github.com/meta ssh_keys; ssh-keygen fingerprints ED25519 +DiY3wvv... and ECDSA p2QAMXNI... match (E1). StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, BatchMode, -F /dev/null. Dropping RSA is fine.

Per vendor-images-only: take the next upstream alpine/git release via Renovate, no derived image. Users: 65534/65534/101, PSA restricted enforced, RO rootfs, drop ALL, seccomp RuntimeDefault, automountServiceAccountToken false.

Kernel v6.18: __fib_validate_source no_addr -> last_resort -> e_rpf for ANY rpf!=0 (fib_frontend.c), so rp_filter 1 drops every IPv4 packet, unicast and multicast, arriving on address-less enp89s0.60. That covers local delivery, forwarding and the normal ARP path, which calls ip_route_input_noref (arp.c L839-840). arp_ignore 8 is load-bearing, not redundant: the sip==0 ARP probe path (arp.c L830-836) never consults rp_filter and would otherwise reply for 172.16.2.82/.83. forwarding 0 gates forwarding and proxy-ARP (arp.c L862). Effective rp_filter/arp_ignore = MAX(all,dev) (inetdevice.h L103/L138), so Cilium's all/rp_filter=0 (base.go:335) cannot weaken them. accept_local/proxy_arp/route_localnet/arp_filter are ORCONF with all=0 and default=0 live, so they stay off. accept_source_route inherits default=1 but it is ANDCONF with all=0, so off. arp_announce is not needed: .60 has no route, so the node never solicits on it. IPsec secpath bypass of rp_filter does not apply (no ipsec). conditions.text: Window definition: W = (max of the 4 KernelParamStatus enp89s0/60 metadata.created, +1 s for resolution) - LinkStatus enp89s0.60 metadata.created. Also report the ms bracket: controller-runtime 'created new link' ts -> last KernelParamSpecController ENOENT ts. Count the ENOENT retries. Cilium attach is recorded as context only. Record timesync: if the node wall clock stepped between link creation and the KPS created time (talosctl get timestatus + controller-runtime/time sync log line), the metadata delta is void and the ms log bracket plus B2 count instead.

Node-side emission counters, read with talosctl read: /proc/net/dev (enp89s0.60 line) + /proc/net/dev_snmp6/enp89s0.60 + /proc/net/if_inet6 + /proc/net/arp. Read (a) in pre-state, (b) as soon as apid answers after reboot, BEFORE uncordon, (c) at step 9. The boot emissions are the (b) values.

UDM capture: capture the VLAN 60 interface UNFILTERED (LAB is near-silent) and apply the node02 MAC filter offline. Keep the CLIENT-VLAN capture filtered on the node02 MAC. Positive controls required: >=1 UDM-originated frame in the VLAN 60 pcap during the reboot, and >=1 node02-MAC frame in the CLIENT-VLAN pcap after the reboot (anchor = NIC up). Record UDM vs node clock (date -u on the UDM + talosctl time) at T_cap_start. Record the port 18 profile (VLAN 60 tagged) and the LAB multicast snooping state. Reconcile: pcap node02-MAC VLAN 60 frames vs (b) tx_packets. pcap < counters = visibility gap, and the counters are authoritative. pcap > counters = FAIL/investigate.

N2/N3 tripwires, read after cilium-agent on node02 is Ready AND again at step 9: v1.sh present 0 FAIL; plus /proc ipv6 all/default disable_ipv6, ipv4 ip_forward, all.forwarding (record); if_inet6 0 lines and arp 0 entries for enp89s0.60; no KernelParamStatus for net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 created AFTER the .60 link (a write to all.* rewrites every device incl .60).

Correct step 8 (G1) and step 10 (G2) in the plan text before the gate. Pre-stated expectation: <=3 IPv6 multicast (MLD) frames from node02 MAC on VLAN 60, all inside W, src :: or fe80::8aae:ddff:fe62:29bf, 0 non-IPv6 frames. Run from the clean kit at a pinned SHA (41992ab or a delta-gated successor).

Any one of these = qa_failed at close and the boot residual is re-rated: (F1) W > 10 s, any of the 4 KPS missing/not current, or W unmeasurable. If 3 s < W <= 10 s, close only with a mitigation item recorded before day 2b admits any LAB host. (F2) any non-IPv6 tx on .60: (b) tx_packets > (b) Ip6OutRequests - Ip6OutDiscards, or any ARP/IPv4 frame from node02 MAC in the VLAN 60 pcap. (F3) > 5 IPv6 frames, or any IPv6 frame other than MLD report / DAD NS / RS, or any src other than :: / the node02 EUI-64 link-local. (F4) any .60 tx increase between (b) and (c), or any node02-MAC VLAN 60 frame later than KPS created + 2 s (after clock-offset correction). (F5) any VLAN 60 frame with IPv4 src 172.16.2.82 or a node02-MAC frame carrying a non-node source IP (= forwarding). (F6) any B4 tripwire value wrong; escalate at once, because this config is live on node02/03. (F7) a B3 positive control is missing AND the B2 counters are unread = INCONCLUSIVE, which does not close N2.

Optional, needs Atlas + Pan because it is active probing: a UDM arping on the LAB interface for 172.16.2.82 at ~5/s across the reboot. This would measure the arp_ignore part of W on the wire. If it is not run, R4/N4 stays the only coverage for ARP/forwarding.

findings.summary: Plan step 8 defines the boot exposure window as 'link -> cilium attached to the parent'. With bpf.vlanBypass [60] live, VID 60 frames bypass all Cilium processing after attach too (bpf_host.c L1206-1211, Argus K6-ok on chg-010). Cilium attach no longer closes anything. The exposure window is link creation -> the last of the 4 per-link sysctls applied, nothing else. Cilium attach is context only.

Plan step 10 says 'expect 0' node frames on VLAN 60. Node counters say otherwise. Since each .60 link was created (both pre-bypass), /proc/net/dev_snmp6/enp89s0.60: node02 Ip6OutRequests=2 Ip6OutMcastPkts=2 Ip6OutDiscards=1, Icmp6OutNeighborSolicits=0, Icmp6OutMLDv2Reports=0 (they failed, so the success counter did not rise); /proc/net/dev enp89s0.60 tx packets=0 tx drop=2. node03: Ip6Out 3/3, discards 2, tx drop=3. Reading: the kernel tried 2-3 IPv6 multicast (MLD) sends on .60 inside the window. The pre-bypass Cilium VLAN_FILTER dropped them. Under vlanBypass [60] the same sends reach the wire. The residual is real, about 2-3 MLD frames per link creation, and has no DAD.

Talos metadata.created/updated have 1 s resolution (LinkStatus enp89s0.60 node03 created 09:49:07Z, all 4 KPS 09:49:08Z). Metadata alone gives the window only as an upper bound. The ms bound comes from controller-runtime 'created new link' and the last KernelParamSpecController ENOENT line.

The UDM capture alone cannot prove 0. The first post-boot node counters are ground truth for emissions from .60, because the counters start at 0 at link creation and the link is recreated at boot. ARP replies and forwarding can only show up if a LAB host sends a stimulus. LAB has none, so they stay covered by R4/N4 and not by this test.

Post-bypass ingress reaches .60: node02 rx 269 pkts / 35 mcast, node03 rx 229. This is a usable positive control that the UDM emits on VLAN 60. igmp6 lists ff02::1/ff02::2/ff01::1 on .60 with disable_ipv6=1. Sends are discarded, so this is not an emission. all/default.disable_ipv6=0, ip_forward=1, all.forwarding=1, .60 forwarding=0, disable_ipv6=1, if_inet6 .60=0, arp .60=0 on both nodes now.

findings.text: Talos resource metadata created/updated are 1 s resolution (live: LinkStatus enp89s0.60 created 2026-10-05T23:20:27Z). Earlier windows were 0.37-0.73 s. Link/KernelParamStatus timestamps alone cannot measure a 1-backoff-step window: they give 0 s or 1 s. Primary sources have to be the controller-runtime log (ms) and dmesg (us monotonic). KernelParamSpecController may log only the ENOENT retries and not the success, so the result is an interval [last ENOENT retry, KPS created + 1 s], not a point.

Step 8 calls link -> cilium attach the boot exposure window. After chg-010, VLAN_FILTER passes VID 60 (bypass [60]), so cilium attach does not end any exposure on .60. Argus ruling 11:16:23Z: the exposure is about 1 KernelParam backoff step. Exposure window = enp89s0.60 oper-up -> the LAST of the 4 sysctls applied (disable_ipv6 for v6, arp_ignore/forwarding/rp_filter for v4). Record cilium attach only as context.

The watchdog will STOP on the reboot itself, not only on z2m: node02-apid NET probe (feeds bump net, which STOPs after 3 samples) and the node02 cilium readiness column. D-a adjudicates only Z2M/Z2M-DEVICES. Second issue: the old day watchdog pid 2427 (morning baseline, until 16:15) shares RUN_DIR/WATCHDOG_STOP with the planned fresh one, so it can re-latch after a clear and judge against a pre-chg-020/pre-HA-restart baseline.

rook-ceph-mon-b is pinned to node02 (nodeSelector). allowMultiplePerNode=false and control planes are tainted, so a Rook mon failover (default mon timeout 10 min) has nowhere to place mon-d. Expect a Pending mon-d plus operator churn if mon-b stays out of quorum for more than 10 min.

The UDM tcpdump on VLAN 60 has no ingress positive control (LAB has 0 clients). If MLD snooping is on, DAD NS to solicited-node multicast may never reach the UDM. A 0-frame result is a lower bound, not proof. A switch-port mirror is a UniFi config write and may reprovision the port, so it is not a fallback today.

M3: clock: record timed sync/step lines from the boot. Compute intra-node deltas from dmesg monotonic, or from controller-runtime lines on the same side of a clock step. Wall-clock deltas across a time step are invalid.

rulings.text: Yes, F1 applies to the UPPER bound of the interval: W_upper = end_upper - start_lower, with start = the earliest timestamped of 'created new link' / .60 up. The plan states end as [last ENOENT, first evidence of all 4 applied]. If no sub-second success line exists, end_upper MAY be KPS created + 1 s. Used as an upper bound that is conservative, so it is not the 'sole end timestamp' F-res forbids. That case is NOT 'unmeasurable' under F1. Report the point estimate only where ms evidence exists. M5 (~1 s pass bar, above = finding) is stricter than my F1 and stands.

Start and end must be in ONE clock domain, or the conversion must be stated. talosctl dmesg wall times are monotonic + boot-time offset. A clock step between the dmesg start and a controller-runtime end makes that cross-domain delta invalid (L60-61 applies to it too).

P6 L33 says 'VLAN 60 has no ingress positive control'. Step 10 L114 requires >=1 UDM-originated frame (0c:ea:14:7a:9d:9b) in the VLAN 60 pcap. Step 10 governs; that frame is the capture-liveness control. 0 node frames remains a lower bound (F-wire), with counters authoritative.

rulings.text: Use --promiscuous on BOTH node03 captures. talosctl pcap defaults to non-promiscuous (talosctl 1.12.6 --help). Without it node03's NIC multicast filter drops what this test is looking for: node02's MLDv2 reports (to 33:33:00:00:00:16) and DAD NS (to 33:33:ff:62:29:bf). node03 has not joined those groups; its .60 igmp6 lists only ff02::1, ff02::2, ff01::1 (boot-plan-review-baseline-2026-10-06.txt). Promisc set on enp89s0.60 also propagates to enp89s0. It is a socket-scoped flag, cleared when the capture ends, so it is not a config write. Record the exact commands.

Do NOT filter node03 enp89s0 on 'ether src 88:ae:dd:62:29:bf' alone. That captures all node02->node03 unicast, including Ceph recovery right after the reboot: a very large stream through apid on the Z-Wave node. Use tcpdump -dd -y EN10MB 'ether src 88:ae:dd:62:29:bf and ether[0] & 1 != 0' (broadcast/multicast only) OR 'ether dst 33:33:00:00:00:16'. The second part is the A-3 control. enp89s0.60 stays unfiltered (LAB ~13 frames/120 s). If node03 watchdog or CPU distress appears, stop the capture first. The counters still decide.

Positive controls. All three are needed for the capture to count; otherwise it is VOID and K-1..K-3 apply. (i) >=1 frame from 0c:ea:14:7a:9d:9b in the node03 .60 pcap during the reboot (liveness of the VLAN 60 path). (ii) >=1 node02 broadcast/multicast frame in the enp89s0 pcap after NIC up (MAC filter + boot anchor). (iii) >=1 frame to 33:33:00:00:00:16 from ANY host in the enp89s0 pcap. This proves unjoined IPv6 multicast reaches node03 in promisc mode, which (i) alone does not. 0 node02 frames on .60 remains a LOWER BOUND (MLD snooping unknown, no flooding proof). The B2 counters stay authoritative.

Timing: read `talosctl time` on node02 AND node03 at capture start and after node02 apid returns. Correct node03 pcap timestamps by the offset before F4 (frames later than window end + 2 s). This replaces the UDM 'date -u' item.

Reconcile the node02-MAC frames in the .60 pcap with B2 (b). pcap > counters = FAIL/investigate (frames with node02 MAC that .60 did not send = spoof or another path). pcap < counters = visibility gap.

Counters-only covers F2, F3, F4 (count part) and F5 (IPv4-src part). F2: (b) tx_packets > Ip6OutRequests - Ip6OutDiscards = non-IPv6 (ARP/IPv4) sent. Any IPv4 src 172.16.2.82 frame on .60 would need a .60 tx, so F2 also catches F5's first clause. F3 typing via the per-device ICMPv6 counters in dev_snmp6/enp89s0.60: (Ip6OutRequests - Ip6OutDiscards) must equal Icmp6OutMLDv2Reports + Icmp6OutNeighborSolicits + Icmp6OutRouterSolicits, or it is an F3 failure. Under vlanBypass the sends succeed, so these per-type counters now increment (pre-bypass they stayed 0 because the sends failed). Also F3 if that total > 5. F3 source address: the only possible IPv6 sources are :: and the EUI-64 link-local, because .60 has no configured or RA address (no address documents; RA off on LAB per chg-008). Accepted on that basis. F4: (b)->(c) any .60 tx increase = FAIL. Also record tx_dropped; it is expected to be 0 under bypass, and anything else is reported.

Without a capture, F4's 'frame after window end + 2 s' clause cannot be tested. Accepted residual: once disable_ipv6=1 is set the kernel discards IPv6 output (counted as Ip6OutDiscards, never tx), and V1 at step 6 proves it is set. IPv4/ARP at any time is caught by F2.

Answer to Atlas: YES, R4/N4 is the backstop for F5 forwarding. Neither counters nor any passive capture can test forwarding: LAB has no host to send to the node02 MAC, and forwarded traffic would leave on enp89s0, not .60. So N2 can close on counters (+ the capture if valid). The R4/N4 active negative test stays binding before day 2b admits ANY LAB host. Also, F7 now means: INCONCLUSIVE if the B2 (b) or (c) reads are missing or the .60 link is absent, regardless of the capture.

rulings.R1_provenance: ACCEPT for mock mode tonight, cosign NOT a pre-deploy blocker. Basis: digest pinned 3/3, own scan, blast radius = PSA restricted, no SA token, no egress, no tenant creds; pods see only the mock key + own CA (pull token is kubelet-only). Signature verify is BINDING before any of: entra-mode commit, any egress allow, any real data, and in any case within 24h of key arrival. FAIL on verify = suspend + delete ns + incident, no re-try on the same digests.
rulings.R1_slsa: ACCEPT as metadata only (self-attested, same key, podman on darwin/arm64 ~L1). It adds no build-integrity assurance beyond the signature; do not cite it as such.
rulings.R1_tlog: ACCEPT --insecure-ignore-tlog=true for this key-signed lab only, IF the fingerprint 6ad2a90a..66e9 is confirmed out of band on a channel not hosted on forge.bluejungle.net (the forge serves both images and cosign.pub@e973b91, so the repo copy alone is not independent; the bundle keyhint is signer-supplied and proves nothing). Lost: no transparency/time evidence, no detection of key misuse. NOT acceptable for target infra (INF-SC-07).
rulings.R2_no_forward_auth: ACCEPT for mock demo: fictional data only, no real names/IDs/TAPs typed in, LAN/VPN only. Re-review mandatory before entra mode.
rulings.R3_shared_store: ACCEPT tonight: no principal that can write ExternalSecrets in lab-passkey lacks cluster-admin already, so the namespace adds no new reader of home-infra. Pre-existing finding stays open; scoped store (or store conditions) REQUIRED before entra mode or any tenant identity/Role in lab-passkey.
rulings.R4_fronting: No new outward risk: web/api/portal have no CNP egress to envoy-internal, so the lab cannot front into the open admin UIs. Inward, the route is unauthenticated by design, so fronting to it gains nothing. inc-2026-09-26-001 stays open and unchanged.

rulings.1_scoped_store: Namespace SecretStore (this commit) is SUFFICIENT for 2026-10-07; the ClusterSecretStore follow-up is NOT required for the demo. Reason: the token Secret in lab-passkey is readable only by principals with secrets/get there (no SA token, no RBAC in the ns, not mounted by any pod) and it reads only vault lab-passkey, i.e. the same values already materialised in that namespace. Residual (pre-existing, R3): live ClusterSecretStore onepassword-connect conditions = namespaceSelector NotIn [mypka] only (kubectl get clustersecretstore onepassword-connect), so ANY ExternalSecret in lab-passkey can read ANY home-infra item; acceptable only because Flux is the sole ES writer. Follow-up F-A (by teardown 2026-10-31 or before any non-synthetic data, whichever first): Heph's ClusterSecretStore pattern AND add lab-passkey to the NotIn list of onepassword-connect, which is the actual gain.
rulings.2_per_workload_secrets: Accepted as built. NEW finding PP-F3 (medium, supplier design, accepted for dev tenant with synthetic users only): the portal (browser-facing) mounts the roster-sync key, and that app identity holds AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All application (src/auth/app-only.ts L3; Graph writes syncAddMember/syncRemoveMember on administrativeUnits, src/graph/allowlist.ts L66-67). The AU is the enrollment population that scopes the backend's TAP right, so a portal compromise = can change who is TAP-eligible. Supplier server.ts L3 calls it 'read-only directory checks' but the credential is not read-only. Report to supplier: portal needs its own read-only app. Not a blocker for the demo.
rulings.3_egress: Verified (see check). Grant is minimal and correct: web login; api/roster/portal login+graph; monitor.azure.com correctly withheld. Residual (inherent): FQDN policy cannot pin a tenant, so login/graph are an outbound channel to ANY Entra tenant; this feeds ruling 5.
rulings.4_no_forward_auth: Acceptable for the lab demo, synthetic users, dev tenant, LAN/VPN-only routes, until teardown. Gate = Entra sign-in to a tenant-specific authority + app-side acrs=c1 check. Conditions R3/R4.
rulings.5_PP-F1_authelia_cookie: Private-window rule still suffices but is now LOAD-BEARING, not hygiene: authelia_session domain = ${SECRET_DOMAIN} (authelia configuration.yaml L31-32, cited on 2026-10-06 qa_passed) so any household browser visiting either hostname hands the SSO cookie to supplier code that in entra mode has an egress path (ruling 3). Rule tightened: demo device uses a private window or a browser profile that has never signed in to Authelia; nobody opens passkey-point-lab / passkey-point-portal-lab in a normal household browser; record the browser state in the E2E evidence. Reverse direction is clean (app cookies host-only, tokens server-side). Durable fix = scope the Authelia cookie (separate, pre-existing).
rulings.6_NODE_ENV_unset: Acceptable (PP_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP is refused with NODE_ENV=production in entra mode, src/tls.ts L49, so unset is required for TLS-at-envoy). (d) client secret allowed (credential.ts L32) -> render refuses by name; R5 adds value check. (e) trustProxy false (app.ts L125, portal/app.ts L70): audit logs record the envoy IP not the client; TAP rate limit is per champion (core.ts L1201) so no limiter collapse; low, accepted. rulings.R3: MET for the push, with a precision gap. The evidence is the owner-run verify summary (out/verify.json 12:33:48Z, 126/0/5/2): 'auth context c1 published', strength 'FIDO2 security key only' fido2 + AAGUID-restricted, policy B app/context+strength+session PASS, state enabled. But no output line names c1 as policy B's target or everyTime as its sign-in frequency; that is Mack's prose ('Meaning:'). S1 (E2E, change does not close without it): for the demo TP sign-in, the Entra sign-in log entry showing appliedConditionalAccessPolicies 'PP-DEV B' result success, authenticationContextClassReferences c1, and the authentication method FIDO2 security key; OR before the push the raw policy JSON (conditions.applications.includeAuthenticationContextClassReferences == [c1], grantControls.authenticationStrength = the FIDO2-only strength id, sessionControls.signInFrequency.frequencyInterval == everyTime, state enabled). S2 NEW, from the evidence: policy B excludes the signed-in admin and targets only the TP / line-manager / list-owner groups. Microsoft documents that ACRS c1 is ISSUED when no policy applies to the user (developer-guide-conditional-access-authentication-context, 'Ariel' table: excluded user requests c1 -> 'c1 (requested)' with no MFA). So the app's acrs=c1 check (src/portal/auth.ts L49-50) only means FIDO2 for members of the targeted groups. Demo rule: the excluded admin account and any account outside the targeted groups is not used for, and not a member of any group/role in, Passkey Point; E2E negative: a non-targeted account must not reach a TAP or portal write action. Any reuse of this design outside the dev tenant = PP-F5 to the supplier (policy B must target All users for c1, admin exclusion via break-glass only).

design.D1_remote: CronJob keeps its name storage/minio-offsite-mirror (collector depends on it). Add an rclone crypt remote AZCRYPT over the existing AZURE remote, env-only like today: RCLONE_CONFIG_AZCRYPT_TYPE=crypt, RCLONE_CONFIG_AZCRYPT_REMOTE=azure:<AZURE_CRYPT_CONTAINER> (set in the script, written as $${AZURE_CRYPT_CONTAINER} because Flux postBuild runs on this Kustomization), FILENAME_ENCRYPTION=standard, DIRECTORY_NAME_ENCRYPTION=true, FILENAME_ENCODING=base32 (rclone default, kept explicit), SUFFIX default. Loop becomes: rclone sync local-minio:$bucket azcrypt:$bucket for cnpg-backups and volsync. The plaintext azure:$${AZURE_CONTAINER} is never written again.
design.D2_new_container: New Azure container offsite-crypt (separate from the existing plaintext container, so the plaintext copy can be removed later as one container and nothing is mixed). rclone azureblob creates it on first upload (the account key has the rights); the drill confirms it exists and is private (public access off). Container name comes from 1P (field AZURE_CRYPT_CONTAINER), same pattern as AZURE_CONTAINER today.
design.D3_compare_mode: Drop --checksum on the crypt sync: crypt exposes no hashes, and rclone falls back to size-only compare, which can miss a rewritten barman backup.info of equal size. Use the default size+modtime with --use-server-modtime kept on the S3 source. To be verified on rclone 1.69.1 in T2 (the second run must transfer 0 unchanged objects, and a touched object must be re-sent).
design.D4_password_handling: rclone needs PASSWORD and PASSWORD2 in obscured form. 1P holds only the PLAIN values. The script obscures them at runtime: export RCLONE_CONFIG_AZCRYPT_PASSWORD=$$(rclone obscure "$${CRYPT_PASSWORD}") (likewise PASSWORD2), never echoed, with set +x. A human can then recover with plain values from 1P and no rclone-specific step.
design.D5_secret_1p: NEW 1P item in vault home-infra: item 'minio-offsite-crypt' (category password/login). Fields: RCLONE_CRYPT_PASSWORD (plain, 64 random chars), RCLONE_CRYPT_PASSWORD2 (salt, plain, 64 random chars), AZURE_CRYPT_CONTAINER (=offsite-crypt), and a notes field with the full recovery recipe: remote type crypt over azureblob:<account>/offsite-crypt, filename_encryption=standard, directory_name_encryption=true, filename_encoding=base32, rclone version used. A separate item, NOT the 'minio' item, because 9 ExternalSecrets across namespaces read 'minio' (root creds); the crypt key goes only to the storage namespace. Generated by the team with op CLI from a random source piped straight into op item create (values never printed or logged, never written to the repo or ops evidence).
design.D6_externalsecret: Keep the pattern: extend the existing ExternalSecret storage/minio-offsite-mirror with three direct-mapped data entries (remoteRef key minio-offsite-crypt, properties RCLONE_CRYPT_PASSWORD, RCLONE_CRYPT_PASSWORD2, AZURE_CRYPT_CONTAINER) into the same target minio-offsite-mirror-secret. No template (multi-line lesson). CronJob env adds CRYPT_PASSWORD / CRYPT_PASSWORD2 / AZURE_CRYPT_CONTAINER via secretKeyRef.
design.D7_offsite_key_copy: Copy 1 offsite = 1Password cloud (the vault is synced to 1Password servers, so it survives loss of the house and cluster) and is only reachable with the owner's 1P Emergency Kit (DR runbook asset #5). Copy 2 MUST be independent of the 1P account, because losing that account loses both the cluster credentials and this key: a printed recovery sheet (both plain values + the notes recipe), sealed, kept OUTSIDE the house in the same place as the owner's 1Password Emergency Kit (e.g. the bank safe-deposit box or a trusted family member's home, whichever holds the Emergency Kit now). The team cannot do this (physical paper, outside the house), so it is an OWNER ACTION. Atlas pushes him one specific instruction once the item exists; the plaintext-purge step (P2) stays blocked until he confirms that copy 2 is in place. No copy in Azure Key Vault or the same storage account: the key would sit next to the data it protects.

Owner really registered in Microsoft Authenticator; Graph returned model '<unknown or invalid>', deviceBound, attested. routeMatches (src/core.ts:1286-1288) recognises Authenticator only by model text. Fix: recognise by aaGuid (iOS 90a3ccdf-635c-4729-a248-9b709135078f, Android de1e552d-db1d-4423-a619-566b625cdc84), model text as fallback; isKey must also exclude the Authenticator AAGUIDs. attack_paths: AP1 password-to-passkey upgrade: anyone who holds an F3R password and has a lenient or compromised TP gets an 8 h multi-use TAP and can register several passkeys. A phished password becomes persistent phishing-resistant access. Sander's 'same risk profile' (L87) compares against the list; the list also required a pre-approved entry, and that is gone.

AP2 bearer TAP at a shared desk: the TAP is shown for 5 min but valid for 480 min and multi-use, and it is a full sign-in method, not only for registration. With D7 (status polling) removed, nothing deletes it after the first registration.
AP3 rate-limit reset: the count is per session (SEC-10.1), so signing in again resets it. 20/h per session gives an unbounded total and no CDC incident below 21.
AP4 eligibility stays cached for the whole session (up to 8 h provisional) after a TP is disabled or loses eligibility, because the per-TAP re-check was dropped.

AP5 Entra session residue: prompt=login forces a credential prompt but does not stop the employee's ESTS cookie from being left in the TP browser. D1 front-channel logout is the only control, and nothing measures it yet.
AP6 lost audit trail: if D11 drops it, misuse below the rate limit can't be detected.

C2 delete the TAP after the first passkey registration is detected (keep D7) OR a CA authentication-strength policy that allows TAP for F3R only from the corporate named location; also test that the TAP is refused as a sign-in from outside that location
C3 keep D10 (key touch per TAP) and D11 (audit trail without ID data); keep v0.9 SEC-02b/10a (TP holds no directory role, checked at sign-in through wids)

C4 AR2 scope openid only (the plan says 'openid profile' at plan L97/L155; names come from Graph anyway); D1 measured by an E02 assertion that no ESTSAUTH* cookie is left for login.microsoftonline.com

answers.q1: Yes. ref.commit takes precedence over branch/tag/semver, so tag moves are inert. Flux does NOT verify signatures (no spec.verify; 96f4589 unsigned); integrity rests on SHA-1 content addressing: go-git hashes received objects, so a force-push cannot change the content of 96f4589. A force-push that drops it from main yields fetch failure = availability only (source keeps last artifact). Residuals: (a) theoretical SHA-1 chosen-prefix collision by the commit author, mitigated by go-git sha1cd (upstream, not verified in this binary) - low; (b) trust now rests on whoever can push vdhinfra main, incl. agents sharing uid 501 - accepted structural, not new.

answers.key_path: execFileSync(openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:3072 -nodes ... -keyout -) with stdio [ignore,pipe,ignore]. Explicit -keyout - overrides any default_keyfile in openssl.cnf; with -out unset, openssl writes key then cert to the inherited fd 1, which node captures into a Buffer. No file path is opened, and /proc/self/fd is no longer used.

It is a read by the app itself, plain $filter on principalId (documented as Example 2 on rbacapplication-list-roleassignments, no advanced query) and a parameterless transitiveMemberOf (advanced query is needed only when query parameters are used). Group-assigned roles carry the group as principalId (groups-concept), which is why (a) alone is not enough and (b) is required.
