rulings.Q1_filtered_projection: ACCEPTED as second layer; B stays required (agree with Atlas). Basis: (a) the filter governs only what vault-tasks holds; it does nothing for vikunja-intents, which carries owner free text and area slugs (my 06:02:01Z finding) and which the bot reads via team 4 today; (b) admission rests on the author's line-1 marking, so a mis-marked file goes out; B makes that residual reach only admforgejo + keys 1/3 instead of a cloud-driven bot; (c) the same public|tier-c marking already gates a cloud-model input (mypka runner, changes.jsonl:2248), so the filter adds no new trust assumption. It answers my 06:02:01Z rejection A (unfiltered tier-a/b) and my C objection (filter dropping only tier-a): it drops a, b, unmarked, non-md, symlinks, non-100644.
rulings.Q2_ledger_names: ACCEPTED, low. Names leak per intent: second-precise timestamp, applied vs rejected, year/month. The 6 hex is random for MacBook intents (vault_core.py:152 secrets.token_hex(3)) but for sync intents it is unsalted sha256(task_id|field|value)[:6] (vikunja_sync.py:509-514, call :608), a 24-bit confirmation oracle on an edited field value. No new disclosure today: the same intent id is already the filename, with full content, in vikunja-intents, whose post-B reader set {admforgejo, key 2/4} is no wider. Condition L1 below.
rulings.Q3_password: YES, block it. Source Forgejo v15.0.9 (live tag 15.0.9). prohibit_login: refuses REST API for any signed-in doer incl. PAT/OAuth2 (routers/api/shared/middleware.go:110, 403), git HTTP (routers/web/repo/githttp.go:173) and SSH (routers/private/serv.go:92,292); kills the token too. Password reset to an unknown value: UserSignIn fails, so basic password path dead; PAT and OAuth2 tokens keep working (services/auth/method/basic.go:71-108 run before password sign-in at :125); token minting needs password auth (permissions/req_basic_or_rev_proxy_auth.go IsPasswordAuthentication), so the bot can no longer mint new PATs. 2FA: TOTP does NOT close it, password + X-Forgejo-OTP header still authenticates (basic.go:143-147,155); WebAuthn would block basic password (:139) but needs a browser login + key as the bot; instance-wide ENABLE_BASIC_AUTHENTICATION=false (:120) would also hit admforgejo's netrc. Recommendation: prohibit_login if Mack confirms the bot has no remaining use after B3 (it then has no team, no org, no registered SSH key, so nothing to use); otherwise password reset to a random >=32-byte value that is generated and discarded, and the password field removed from the 1P item.
rulings.Q4_deploy_key_2: YES. Delete now (unused: no clone, env unset, no --forge in morning run, per Mack). Deploy keys are per-repo, so re-adding is scoped by construction. Re-add as its own change when the forge drain goes live; RW is then justified (bord_drain.py:122 pushes ledger deletions). Prefer a fresh key at re-add over re-registering SHA256:gxGK2Kxi...; leave the private key file in place (no rm).
rulings.Q5_B2: YES, unblocked for today. My 06:09:15Z phasing put B2 on the CronJob-unsuspend/T3 path only for lack of Mack's reader answer; he has given it (no bot reader on their side). B3 (org removal) follows once team 4 repos=[] and members check done.
rulings.Q6_BA3: One token is enough to prove B's repo-reach removal, because every credential of a user is bounded by that user's permission, and the BA2 Sudo matrix measures exactly that. One token is NOT enough to prove the bot has no other live credential: OAuth2 access tokens authenticate via basic too (basic.go:71) and do not appear in the PAT listing, and the PAT listing endpoint itself needs password auth. So BA3's listing stays, extended per C4.

adr028_positions.D1: security prefers single-use: a multi-use 480-min pass is replayable for 8 h and TAP-issued tokens live until its expiry. Cost (second desk visit) is the owner's trade-off. Owner words required; no change without them
adr028_positions.D2: more permissive than requested (longer or multi-use when single asked) -> do not show, send remove, read back, security audit event; less permissive -> show. Plus range check (F3). Owner words required
adr028_positions.D3: 95.3 bits is ADEQUATE. Online at 1e6 guesses/s over a 300 s TTL: 3e8/62^16 (4.77e28) = ~6e-21. Even offline vs unsalted SHA-256 at 1e12/s for 300 s: ~6e-15. Entropy is not the weak link; disclosure is (F6, F2). Adequacy assumes service-side single use, expiry in minutes, UPN binding and app-token authentication on retrieve; if the spec shows any of these absent, re-review. No objection to replacing the 128-bit brief; needs the AGR register entry
adr028_positions.D4: separate identity strongly preferred; enforce separation from our own app ids now (F4)
adr028_positions.D5_D6_D7_D9: current defaults are the safe ones (no remove-before-create, no resend after send, failed=definite only if the spec confirms nothing is left behind, no restart)

adr029_conditions: B1 own app registration, exactly one application permission UserAuthMethod-TAP.ReadWrite.All; start-up self-check on its token's roles (exact set) and the F1-F6 wids rule; its role id added to the P4 tripwire: every other component's self-check refuses a token that carries it (test)

B2 time-bounded grant (P3 pattern): the role assignment is granted at the start of an E2E run and DELETED at its end, read back absent, and a fresh token proven to no longer carry it. No standing grant between runs. Credential expiry is only the backstop

B3 target allowlist = option (c): fixed persona (object id, UPN) pairs written by bootstrap-v01; Graph calls addressed by the listed oid, never by a caller-supplied UPN. The list must not be writable at runtime by any devtenant service account (bake into the image or a Flux-owned ConfigMap; prove with kubectl auth can-i for every SA in the ns)

B4 strike the clause 'still refuses if Graph's TAP call reports the user holds a role': Graph does no such check for app-only callers (ADR-027 K2 created a pass for the dev admin). Role check = ops app (read-only) at the START of every E2E run (fail closed) plus nightly

B5 admin deny by object id in code (UPNs can be renamed), not by UPN in config; plus the Entra TAP method policy includeTargets = persona group only and excludeTargets = admin + any role holder. This is a PRECONDITION, but per Microsoft Learn ('Although you can create a TAP for any user, only users included in the policy can sign in with it') it blocks SIGN-IN, not CREATION: fix the ADR wording ('Entra refuses a pass for anyone else' is wrong). The persona group must not be role-assignable and the sim identity must hold no group or policy write right

B6 lifetime: the ADR's '60 minutes (the Entra minimum)' is wrong; Entra allows 10-43,200 min, the floor is the tenant policy's minimumLifetime (default 1 h). Use the dev-tenant policy floor, lower that floor to <=15 min if it does not break other dev flows, fixed in code; isUsableOnce true fixed in code

B7 value: memory only, keyed by code hash, dropped at retrieve or 5-min code expiry, on expiry remove the pass with read back; never logged (leak test with fake Graph, as planned); Graph request-id logged only
B8 remove read back as written (list methods again; remove_not_confirmed on failure); teardown sweep over pp-e2e- personas stays
B9 dev tenant pinned in code: authority tenant AND token tid must equal DEV_TENANT; not overridable by config; refuse otherwise (test)

B10 credential: workload identity preferred. Certificate fallback ACCEPTED, but fix the contradiction in section 6 ('generated in the cluster and never leaves it' vs 'ExternalSecret from 1Password'): pick one and state it truthfully. Validity <=30 days, rotation = change record with removal read back, never a client secret

B11 transport: in mode B a real pass crosses api->sim, so plain HTTP inside the ns is not acceptable: TLS on the listener or mTLS; auth.mode entra mandatory; allowedClientIds non-empty (api TAP identity + E2E runner only)

B12 tripwire on use: the ops app reads the tenant audit log after each run and nightly; any TAP create/delete by the sim SP outside a run window or for a target not on the list opens an incident; kill switch (credential/app delete) tested once before first use

On Apple VZ that means Rosetta = VZLinuxRosettaDirectoryShare, a virtiofs share: Apple doc 'directory share exposes the Rosetta directory from the host file system to the guest'. Contradicts V0 (no virtiofs) and adds a host virtiofs surface to a VM where every job is root (automount socket). rulings.a_udp443_kpn: ACCEPT. WireGuard answers nothing without a valid MAC1 (needs server pubkey), so UDP 443 has the same unauthenticated surface as 51820/51821 today. Net surface shrinks: 51821 leaves Ziggo. No existing 443 forward/listener (M6: forwards are only tcp80, tcp_udp61952, tcp32400). Moving off Ziggo is correct (KPN is effective primary; VDHNGFW had 0 events since 2026-09-22). Caveat: VDHNGFW today has vpn_binding_mode any -> must be pinned to wan2.
rulings.b_peer_scope: Same-as-VDHVPN02 = Vpn zone allow-all to Internal (CLIENT 172.16.2.0/23 + SERVER 172.16.10.0/23, incl UDM .1, VIP .240 kube/talos API, NAS .246), Gateway (UDM UI + password ssh), Vpn (peer-to-peer), Hotspot, Dmz; IoT and Lab blocked (evidence chg-2026-10-05-008/after-step3-policies.json, 2026-10-05 snapshot). There is no separate management VLAN, so least privilege must be IP/port based, scoped to src 192.168.12.0/24 so VDHVPN02 is untouched. Mudi is a travel router that bridges arbitrary hotel-side devices: it must get the minimum. c2_rule_v2.rule: Header H = -----BEGIN [A-Z ]*(SIGSTORE|COSIGN) PRIVATE KEY-----, end E = -----END [A-Z ]*(SIGSTORE|COSIGN) PRIVATE KEY-----, separator S = any run of space, tab, CR, LF or literal backslash-escaped n/r ((?:[ \t\r\n]|\\+[nr])*). For every file listed by grep -rIlE H: total = number of H matches, synthetic = number of matches of H S FAKEKEYBODY S E (perl -0777, global count), real = total - synthetic. c2_rule_v2.why_it_cannot_hide_a_key: a block passes only when its entire body is the 11-character token FAKEKEYBODY directly followed by the END line. A real cosign/sigstore key body is base64 of an encrypted envelope, hundreds of characters long; 11 characters is not a valid base64 length and cannot carry a key. Otherwise use a no-admin alternative, such as a separate package namespace plus a pin change by Mack. The 07:00 deadline is not a security reason: v7 stays live.

answers.Q1: envoy-internal only; drop 8123 and the toEntities host/remote-node rule. Live: route home-assistant-main parent=envoy-internal (LAN-only since chg-2026-10-05-020, remote via Nabu Casa), so .241:443 already reaches HA. host/remote-node:8123 grants every node netns incl. control planes on 8123, and HA trusts X-Forwarded-For from 10.42.0.0/16 + 172.16.2.0/23, which is where the masqueraded source lands. Remove 8123 from the in-pod nft set and from T1 positives. Delete the inert UniFi 10002 8123 policy together with the other WG443 policies (F5).
answers.Q2: No GitHub Actions secret on the public repo. Public logs + third-party actions + Renovate automerge = one compromised action publishes the key; zero-scope is enforced only by the in-pod nft in the same pod. Alternative: T3 attended on Sunday from the MacBook or iPhone on MOBILE DATA (hotspot, wifi off), which is a real internet path and gives the same non-RFC1918 endpoint proof. Unattended outside canary only via (a) a separate PRIVATE repo with run:-only steps, actions pinned by SHA, no PR/pull_request_target triggers, environment-scoped secret, or (b) a VPS (money, owner). No Ziggo-to-KPN loop: the UDM delivers its own WAN2 address locally, so that is a hairpin.
answers.Q4: Measure first: V0 cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward in a plain pod on node01 (IPv4 conf inherits from init_net by default, and Talos sets 1). If 1: no init container and no sysctl at all. If 0: privileged init container accepted (one-shot, same digest-pinned image, fixed command sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1, no volumes, no SA token), not Talos allowedUnsafeSysctls (node-wide policy relaxation and a rolling worker change).
